title: Manual DNA Extraction using Qiagen DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit
author: Julie Haendiges
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bi4dkgs6
materials: Qiagen DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit
Discard the collection tube and its contents.

steps.title: Prepare Enzymatic Lysis Buffer (ELB) Stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a 250 mL stock of enzymatic lysis buffer (ELB) containing 20 mM Tris-HCl, 2 mM EDTA, and 1.2% Triton.

substeps.instruction: Mix 5 mL of 1 M Tris-HCl, 1 mL of 0.5 M EDTA, and 3 mL of Triton X-100.
Add molecular-grade water to bring the total volume to 250 mL.
Mix gently to incorporate the Triton.
Store at room temperature (stable for 1 year).

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer with Enzymes
steps.instruction: Add lysozyme to the lysis buffer within 24 hours of use.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 mg/ml of lysozyme to the appropriate amount of lysis buffer.
For Staphylococcus spp., add 1 mg of lysostaphin for every 2 ml of ELB, regardless of preparation method.

steps.title: Harvest Bacterial Cells
steps.instruction: Collect and pellet the bacterial cells from the culture.

substeps.instruction: Remove inoculated TSB samples from the incubator.
Resuspend cells in the bacterial culture by pulse vortexing 3-5 times on low setting or by pipetting.
Transfer 1.0 mL of bacterial culture into a 2.0 mL sterile Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge at 7500 rpm for 5 minutes to pellet cells.
Discard supernatant into a 50 mL conical tube containing 10% commercial bleach marked 'biohazard waste'.

steps.title: Perform Bacterial Lysis
steps.instruction: Select appropriate lysing conditions based on bacteria type and treat the cell pellet.

substeps.instruction: Add 180 µL of Buffer ATL (if precipitate is present, warm to 56 °C until dissolved) OR add 180 µL of enzymatic lysis buffer (ELB) + Enzyme to the sample tube.
Resuspend the bacterial cell pellet by vortexing.
Incubate at 56 °C for 30 minutes.
Add 25 µL of Proteinase K and 200 µL of Buffer AL.
Vortex on high setting for 5 seconds to mix.
Incubate at 56 °C for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Purify DNA and Remove RNA
steps.instruction: Prepare the lysate for binding and remove RNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 100% Ethanol and mix by vortexing.
Add 4 µL of RNase A, mix by vortexing, and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Spin Column
steps.instruction: Transfer the treated cells to a DNeasy spin column to bind the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Label the lid of a DNeasy spin column with a unique, recorded identifier for each sample.
Using a P1000 pipette, transfer the full volume of pre-treated bacterial cells to the corresponding spin column.
Centrifuge at 8000 rpm (> 6000 x g) for 1 minute.

steps.title: Wash DNA Bound to Column
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA using Buffer AW1 and AW2.

substeps.instruction: Place the spin column into a new 2.0 mL collection tube.
Add 500 µL of Buffer AW1.
Centrifuge at 8000 rpm (> 6000 x g) for 1 minute.
Place the spin column into a new 2.0 mL collection tube.
Add 500 µL of Buffer AW2.
Centrifuge at 13000 rpm (> 20000 x g) for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Dry Spin Column
steps.instruction: Ensure no residual wash buffer remains on the column.

substeps.instruction: Examine the spin column to ensure no liquid remains; if liquid is present, repeat the final centrifugation step until clean.

steps.title: Elute Purified DNA
steps.instruction: Elute the purified DNA into a sterile tube.

substeps.instruction: Place the spin column in a new, sterile 1.5 mL elution tube labeled with a unique identifier and/or FDA accession (CFSANxxxxxx) number.
Add 100 µL of Buffer EB to the spin column (Optional: Incubate Buffer EB at 37 °C prior to addition to improve elution).
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at 8000 rpm (> 6000 x g) for 1 minute.

steps.title: Store Purified DNA
steps.instruction: Collect the eluate and store according to duration requirements.

substeps.instruction: Retain the eluate as the purified DNA.
Store at 4 °C for short-term storage.
Store at -20 °C or -80 °C for long-term storage.
